# A molecule franchise that no single reporting level shows

Cilnidipine is an L/N-type calcium channel blocker positioned clinically as an
alternative to amlodipine, with a lower reported incidence of pedal oedema. In
the supplied dataset it appears in several places at once: as a plain CCB, as a
component of dual fixed-dose combinations with an angiotensin receptor blocker
and with beta blockers, and inside triple combinations with a diuretic.

Because those entries sit in different sub-segments, no single row of the
standard reporting hierarchy shows the size of the franchise. The
anchor-molecule space level in this agent exists specifically to make it
visible - it sums every pack containing the molecule regardless of where the
audit files it.

Two structural facts follow from the data and are worth stating plainly. The
plain molecule is concentrated in one corporate group's brand. The combinations
built on it are markedly less concentrated, and the triple combinations are the
least concentrated of all.

## Why this matters for prioritisation

The competitive question is not "can we enter cilnidipine" - it is "at which
layer of the cilnidipine franchise is share still being allocated". Attacking
the plain molecule means attacking an entrenched leader head-on. Entering the
combination layer means competing in spaces where no player has consolidated a
defensible position.

This signal is derived from the case dataset itself rather than from external
publication, and is labelled as such. It is included because the case asks the
agent to identify "other relevant market clusters", and this is the clearest
example of one.
